artifacts.summary: 9-phase plan rebasing load_when.agents hooks onto real @-reference sets across four index-entries.json files, then replacing the stale inert EXCEPTIONS block in validate-context-budgets.sh with three accurately measured per-agent exceptions. Target: 8 violations -> 0 with 3 documented OK* rows, no CAPS raised.

memory_candidates.content: Deployed .claude/context/index.json can carry ghost entries with no source-store owner. install-extension.sh's merge_index_entries uses purely additive `.entries += ...`, and the lua deploy engine's remove_orphaned_index_entries is keyed on content-file existence under context_dir. So when a context file is renamed, BOTH the stale index entry and the stale deployed content file survive indefinitely, and the ghost keeps contributing tokens to whatever agent its load_when.agents named. Observed concretely: orchestration/orchestration-validation.md (1,864 tok, hooked to meta-builder-agent) and orchestration/subagent-validation.md (2,504 tok) exist only in the deployed index while the source store has orchestration/validation.md. Practical consequence for any task that edits index-entries.json to change per-agent budgets: the sum of edited source entries will NOT equal what validate-context-budgets.sh reports, because that script reads the deployed index. Always set-difference the deployed index's path set against the union of all agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json path sets first, and carry the resulting per-agent offset as a known constant through every later measurement.
